gen-02-dias.context: Genesis 1:2 ends with the earth formless and empty. From there, the account moves day by day with repeated marks: God speaks, what he said happens, God sees that it is good, and the day closes with evening and morning.
gen-02-dias.focusQuestion: What part of your life do you need God to bring order to today?
gen-02-dias.keywordGloss: On the first days, God separates light and darkness, waters and waters, sea and land: each thing gets its place.
reflectionPrompts: God sees that it is good
facts: God separates the light from the darkness.
God calls the expanse Heavens.
God tells the waters to gather so the dry land appears.
God makes the two great lights and also the stars.
God blesses the sea creatures and the birds.
God looks at the animals he made and sees that it is good.

gen-08-caim.context: Outside Eden, Adam and Eve have two sons: Cain, who works the ground, and Abel, who keeps sheep (Gen 4:1–2). One day, the two brothers bring offerings to the Lord.
gen-08-caim.focusQuestion: What feeling is "at the door" of your heart today, waiting to be mastered?
gen-08-caim.keywordGloss: God describes sin as something crouching at the entrance, desiring Cain; even so, Cain can and must master it.
facts: Cain brought an offering to the Lord from the fruit of the ground.
Abel brought some of the firstborn of his flock.
Cain was very angry, and his face fell.
God told Cain that sin was at the door.
Cain killed Abel in the field.
God asked Cain where Abel was.

gen-10-babel.context: After the flood, God blessed Noah and his sons: "fill the earth" (9:1). The families multiply, but part of humanity decides to stay together in one place and build something for themselves.
gen-10-babel.focusQuestion: In what area of your life have you been trying to make a name without depending on God?
gen-10-babel.keywordGloss: The ambition to secure fame and safety without God; in Genesis 12:2, it is God who promises to make Abram's name great.
facts: The whole earth had a single language.
They made bricks and used tar for mortar.
They wanted a tower whose top would reach the heavens.
They wanted to make a name for themselves.
The Lord came down to see the city and the tower.
The city was named Babel.

gen-11-abraao.context: Genesis 11 ends with the peoples scattered and Terah's family settled in Haran. Sarai, Abram's wife, was barren and had no children (11:30). In this setting, with no future in sight, God speaks.
gen-11-abraao.focusQuestion: What might God be calling you to leave behind in order to trust him?
gen-11-abraao.keywordGloss: God promises to bless Abram and make him a channel of blessing for all the families of the earth.
reflectionPrompts: The blessing is for all families
facts: The Lord told Abram to leave his land, his relatives and his father's house.
The land would still be shown to Abram.
God promised to make Abram a great nation.
In Abram, all the families of the earth would be blessed.
Abram left as the Lord had told him, and Lot went with him.
Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

gen-boss-01.context: This challenge reviews creation, from Genesis 1:1 to 2:3. The account has a rhythm: God speaks, it happens, God sees that it is good. At the end of the sixth day, God gives food to all and looks at the whole work.
gen-boss-01.focusQuestion: If God rules and sustains all he has made, what can you entrust to him today?
gen-boss-01.keywordGloss: At the end of the sixth day, God's verdict rises: not just good, but very good.
facts: God calls the dry land Earth and the gathered waters Seas.
God makes the two great lights and also the stars.
God blesses the sea creatures and the birds.
God gives human beings plants and fruit trees for food.
To the animals, God gives every green plant.
God sees that everything he made was very good.

gen-01-criador.context: Genesis was written for a people surrounded by stories in which the world is born from a war between gods. The Bible's first sentence goes the other way: before everything, there is one God, and he creates.
gen-01-criador.focusQuestion: What changes in your day when you start with God, and not with yourself?
gen-01-criador.keywordGloss: In the text, only God is the subject of the verb create: he brings into being what did not exist.
facts: God is the one who creates the heavens and the earth.
In the beginning, the earth was formless and empty.
There was darkness over the face of the deep.
The Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.
God speaks, and light comes to be.

gen-03-imagem.context: After filling sky, sea and land, the account reaches human beings. Here God does something he had not done before: he announces his decision before creating and then speaks directly to those he made.
gen-03-imagem.focusQuestion: How would you treat people today if you remembered that each one bears the image of God?
gen-03-imagem.keywordGloss: Human beings, male and female, were made to reflect who God is and to care for the world on his behalf.
facts: God decides to make man in his image and likeness.
Human beings receive dominion over fish, birds and animals.
The verb "criou" appears three times in Genesis 1:27.
God creates male and female.
God blesses the man and the woman and speaks to them.

gen-04-descanso.context: After six days of work, God saw that everything was very good (Gen 1:31). Now the account reaches the seventh day and, for the first time, God creates nothing new.
gen-04-descanso.focusQuestion: What would change in your week if you stopped, trusting that God sustains what you leave unfinished?
gen-04-descanso.keywordGloss: In the text, God rests because he finished the work, not because he was tired: it is stopping before what is complete.
facts: The heavens, the earth and all their host were completed.
God finished his work on the seventh day.
God rested from all the work he had done.
God blessed the seventh day and made it holy.
The text calls God the Creator.

gen-05-eden.context: After forming the man from the dust of the ground (Gen 2:7), the account draws closer: the Lord God prepares a place for him. The garden appears with trees, a river that waters it, and names of lands and rivers.
gen-05-eden.focusQuestion: What part of your work today can you do as care for what God has entrusted to you?
gen-05-eden.keywordGloss: Making the land bear fruit and protecting it: the calling God gives human beings before any disobedience.
facts: The Lord God planted a garden in Eden.
God placed in the garden the man he had formed.
The trees were pleasing to the eye and good for food.
The tree of life was in the middle of the garden.
A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden.
God put the man in the garden to work it and keep it.

gen-06-queda.context: In the garden, God had given wide freedom and a single limit, with a clear warning (Gen 2:16–17). Now a new voice appears in the garden: the serpent. And the conversation starts with what God said.
gen-06-queda.focusQuestion: At what point in your day are you tempted to doubt that God wants your good?
gen-06-queda.keywordGloss: The serpent begins by asking what God said and ends by saying the opposite of what he said.
facts: The serpent was craftier than all the wild animals.
The serpent asks whether God forbade eating from every tree in the garden.
The serpent claims they will not die.
The woman sees that the tree is good for food and pleasing to the eye.
Her husband was with her, and he ate too.

gen-07-consequencias.context: After the disobedience, God questioned the man and the woman, and each passed the blame along. Now God speaks in reverse order: first to the serpent, then to the woman and, finally, to the man.
gen-07-consequencias.focusQuestion: Where do you see the consequences of sin today, and where do you see God's promise?
gen-07-consequencias.keywordGloss: Hostility that God himself sets between the serpent and the woman: evil will have no peace, and the fight will go on until victory.
reflectionPrompts: Promise in the midst of judgment
facts: The serpent is declared cursed among all the animals.
God puts hostility between the serpent and the woman.
The woman's offspring will strike the serpent's head.
The woman will give birth to children in pain.
The ground is cursed because of the man.
The man will return to the dust he was formed from.

gen-09-diluvio.context: After Cain, Genesis shows violence passing from generation to generation. The flood account begins with God's view of the human heart and ends with God committing himself to the earth.
gen-09-diluvio.focusQuestion: Where do you need to hear today that God takes sin seriously and still offers grace?
gen-09-diluvio.keywordGloss: A commitment God makes on his own initiative: after the flood, he binds himself to the earth and to living things with a sign.
reflectionPrompts: Grace in the midst of judgment
facts: The Lord saw that human wickedness was multiplying on the earth.
Every intention of the human heart was only evil all the time.
Human wickedness grieved the Lord's heart.
Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord.
Noah walked with God.
God set the bow in the clouds as the sign of the covenant.

gen-boss-02.context: This challenge revisits Genesis 2 and 3: the garden God planted, the command about the tree, the conversation with the serpent, the hiding, God's questions and the departure from Eden.
gen-boss-02.focusQuestion: In what part of your life do you try to hide from God instead of answering when he calls?
gen-boss-02.keywordGloss: It stands in the middle of the garden from the start; after the fall, the way to it is guarded by God.
facts: God planted a garden in Eden and placed the man there.
God forbade eating from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
The serpent told the woman they would not die.
After eating, the couple hid from God among the trees.
God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife.
Cherubim were set to guard the way to the tree of life.

gen-boss-final.context: Genesis 1–11 tells the story of the world before Abram: a good creation, disobedience, violence, the flood and Babel. Genesis 12 opens a new way. This challenge follows the whole thread.
gen-boss-final.focusQuestion: In what part of your story do you need to remember that God has not given up on you?
gen-boss-final.keywordGloss: God's word that opens a future: from the announced defeat of the serpent (3:15) to blessing for all the families of the earth (12:3).
reflectionPrompts: Sin breaks, but does not win
facts: God created the heavens and the earth.
God saw all that he had made, and it was very good.
The woman ate the fruit and gave some to her husband, who ate too.
Cain rose up against Abel and killed him.
At Babel, the people wanted to make a name for themselves.
In Abram, all the families of the earth would be blessed.
